sourceOccurrences.note: 4K33 proves the signed degree identity and branch-versus-leaf bounds, including the empty forest and isolated vertices. The correction by twice the number of non-singleton components is an additional consequence of the source identity. A finite-tree leaf-containing set must have at least two vertices. The source proves no encounter-point construction or probabilistic uniqueness theorem.

proofUses.reason: Unique paths give connection probabilities; summing over the two directions gives susceptibility. The finite-size law uses prescribed-cluster factorization.
Every finite unit-rate intensity produces a bond probability strictly below one, so neither percolating parameter set has a finite member.
